findings.evidence: The address now comes from ClientAddress.resolve, which takes the LAST X-Forwarded-For entry (the one Nginx appended) and falls back to the socket address. ClientAddressTest and AuthControllerPasswordResetTest cover forged leading entries.
findings.why_it_matters: The per-address limit can no longer be dodged or aimed at another user's address with a forged header.

findings.evidence: The endpoint now only validates and enqueues; lookup, token write and mail run on a private bounded pool that discards when full and swallows failures without logging the address. PasswordResetDispatcherTest shows the service has not run when requestAsync returns. The executor is deliberately not an Executor bean, so Spring Boot's default task executor stays active.
findings.why_it_matters: Response time no longer depends on whether the address has an account.
findings.required_action: None. The spec's '<50 ms median difference' criterion still needs a timing measurement against a running stack.

findings.evidence: Docker is not running on this machine, so the Testcontainers-based Postgres tests were skipped and V16/V17 were never executed against PostgreSQL; they were reviewed by hand only.
findings.why_it_matters: A syntax or constraint-name mistake would only surface at first deployment.
findings.required_action: Run the app against a disposable PostgreSQL (or the Postgres test profile with Docker up) before merging.
